title: Fibres of the affine groupoid invariant spectrum are orbits
statement: Let $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $R=\operatorname{Spec}B$ be affine schemes [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Suppose $s,t:R\to U$, $e:U\to R$, $i:R\to R$ and $c:R\times_{s,U,t}R\to R$ [def-pc-fibre-product] are morphisms such that, functorially in every test scheme $H$, $U(H)$ is the object set and $R(H)$ the arrow set of a groupoid with source $s$, target $t$, identity $e$, inverse $i$ and composition $c$. Write $\sigma=s^\sharp,\tau=t^\sharp:A\to B$ and $C=\{a\in A:\sigma(a)=\tau(a)\}$. Assume $s,t$ are finite locally free [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. For $M=\operatorname{Spec}C$, the canonical map $|U|\to|M|$ is surjective. Two points $u_0,u_1\in|U|$ have the same image in $|M|$ if and only if there exists $r\in|R|$ with $s(r)=u_0$ and $t(r)=u_1$. Moreover, for every algebraically closed field $k$, the map $U(k)\to M(k)$ is surjective and its fibres are exactly the equivalence classes generated by $s,t:R(k)\rightrightarrows U(k)$.
